rationale: The technical pain is real — blind scrubbing over a long DVR window is a known streaming infrastructure problem — but the buyer is a streaming infrastructure engineer at a media tech company, a small and highly technical ICP that typically builds in-house, contributes to open source, or uses existing CDN-level tooling (Cloudflare Stream, Mux, AWS MediaLive) that already bundles thumbnail sprites. Willingness to pay for a standalone service on top of their existing CMAF pipeline is weak. More critically, the solution itself requires deep media processing infrastructure (real-time sprite sheet generation, CMAF segment inspection, WebVTT indexing) that goes well beyond Claude prompts + a web form — this needs custom backend code, media pipeline expertise, and significant ongoing compute, none of which a solo non-technical operator can build or maintain with this factory's tooling. The autonomy and buildability scores both fail their build gate floors decisively.
solution_plan: A solo non-technical operator using this factory cannot realistically build or maintain this service. It requires real-time video segment processing, sprite sheet generation from decoded frames, CMAF muxing logic, and CDN integration — none of which Claude or standard web tooling handles. The buyer (streaming infrastructure engineers) would expect a robust, low-latency media processing backend, and would not pay for a wrapper around general AI capabilities. Dropping this opportunity is the correct call; if the operator has a specific media-tech background or partnership, revisit with a co-founder who can own the infrastructure layer.
notes: Fails multiple build gates: buildability_with_ai=3 (below min 6), operational_autonomy=4 (below min 7), buyer_clarity=5 (below min 6), willingness_to_pay=4 (below min 5). Recommended stage: drop. This is an engineering infrastructure problem, not an AI-augmented service problem.
